# Cardinality of Triangular Subsets of the Sierpiński Triangle

## Key Property of the Sierpiński Triangle

The Sierpiński triangle $S$ is constructed as:
$$S = \bigcap_{n=0}^{\infty} S_n$$
where $S_n$ is the union of $3^n$ solid equilateral triangles of side length $2^{-n}$.

**Empty Interior:** The Lebesgue measure of $S_n$ is $(3/4)^n \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$, so $S$ has Lebesgue measure zero. Since any non-empty open set in $\mathbb{R}^2$ has positive measure, **$S$ has empty interior** — it contains no open disk, and hence no 2-dimensional region.

## Identifying Triangular Subsets

A (non-degenerate) filled triangle $T$ in $\mathbb{R}^2$ contains an open disk (it has positive 2-dimensional Lebesgue measure and non-empty interior).

For $T$ to be a **triangular subset** of $S$, we require:
$$T \subseteq S$$

But since $T$ contains an open set (a small disk $B \subset T$), this would force:
$$B \subseteq T \subseteq S$$

This contradicts the fact that $S$ has empty interior (contains no open disk).

## Conclusion

No non-degenerate filled triangle can be a subset of the Sierpiński triangle. The collection of all triangular subsets of $S$ is therefore the **empty set**.

$$|\{T : T \text{ is a triangle and } T \subseteq S\}| = |\varnothing| = 0$$

$$\boxed{0}$$
